policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: Both prepositions render as 'unto' before Bethphage; ASV's 'came unto Bethphage' does not distinguish εἰς from πρὸς.
The Greek article on a personal name is not rendered in English; ASV 'then Jesus sent' is identical under either reading.
ASV 'Go into the village' renders either imperative form; middle Πορεύεσθε and passive-deponent Πορεύθητε are indistinguishable in English.
κατέναντι and ἀπέναντι are synonymous; ASV 'that is over against you' does not choose between them.
εὐθέως and εὐθὺς are the same adverb; ASV 'straightway ye shall find' renders either.
English imperative 'bring them unto me' marks no aspect, so aorist ἀγάγετέ and present ἄγετέ are not distinguished.
εὐθὺς and εὐθέως are the same adverb; ASV 'and straightway he will send them' renders either.
ASV 'he will send them' is future, matching future ἀποστελεῖ rather than present ἀποστέλλει ('he sendeth').
ASV reads 'Now this is come to pass' with no rendering of ὅλον ('all this'), so the added word is absent from the text translated.
ASV renders the preposition explicitly a second time — 'And upon a colt the foal of an ass' — which the reading omitting ἐπὶ would not supply.
συνέταξεν and προσέταξεν both yield ASV 'even as Jesus appointed them'; the compound is not distinguished in English.
ἐπ᾽ αὐτῶν and ἐπάνω αὐτῶν alike give ASV 'put on them their garments'.
ASV 'their garments' is idiomatic English for the articular ἱμάτια as well as for ἱμάτια αὐτῶν; the possessive is not italicized either way, so it settles nothing.
ASV 'the multitudes that went before him' renders the object αὐτὸν, which the omitting reading lacks.
ASV keeps the appositional order of the base — 'This is the prophet, Jesus, from Nazareth' — with the title first and the name in apposition, not 'Jesus the prophet'.
The article on Ἰησοῦς is not rendered; ASV 'And Jesus entered' is the same under either reading.
ASV prints 'the temple of God' in the text and notes 'Many ancient authorities omit of God', so it renders the reading with τοῦ θεοῦ added.
ASV 'but ye make it a den of robbers' is present, matching ποιεῖτε rather than aorist ἐποιήσατε ('ye made it').
ASV 'the blind and the lame' follows the order τυφλοὶ καὶ χωλοὶ, not the transposed 'lame and blind'.
English requires 'the children' whether or not the Greek article stands, so ASV does not distinguish presence of τοὺς.
Πρωῒ and πρωΐας are the same temporal expression; ASV 'Now in the morning' renders either.
ASV 'as he returned to the city' fits a present participle and equally a coincident aorist participle; the English marks no anteriority that would exclude ἐπαναγαγὼν.
The added οὐ only strengthens the negation, which English renders the same way; ASV 'Let there be no fruit from thee henceforward for ever' fits both.
ἂν and ἐὰν are interchangeable in the indefinite relative clause; ASV 'whatsoever ye shall ask' renders either.
Genitive absolute and dative participle both yield ASV 'And when he was come into the temple'; the case of the participle leaves no English trace.
English 'The baptism of John' is definite with or without the Greek article, so its presence is not distinguished.
ἐν ἑαυτοῖς and παρ᾽ ἑαυτοῖς alike give ASV 'they reasoned with themselves'.
English word order here is fixed — 'all hold John as a prophet' — and cannot mirror the fronting of ὡς προφήτην, so the transposition is not distinguished.
ASV coordinates the clause — 'A man had two sons; and he came to the first, and said' — rendering the conjunction καὶ that the asyndetic base reading lacks.
ASV reads 'go work to-day in the vineyard' with no possessive; the added μου ('my vineyard') is unrendered.

ASV 'I will not: but afterward he repented himself, and went' renders the Οὐ θέλω reading and excludes r02 ('I go, sir; and went not'); r00-base and r01 are the same words and differ only in printed punctuation.
δὲ and καὶ are both rendered 'And' at the head of the clause; ASV 'And he came to the second' does not distinguish them.
ASV 'he came to the second' renders the ordinal δευτέρῳ, not ἑτέρῳ ('the other').
ASV 'I go, sir: and went not' renders the Ἐγώ, κύριε reading and excludes r02 ('I will not... afterward he repented'); r00-base and r01 are the same words and differ only in printed punctuation.
ASV reads simply 'They say, The first', with no 'unto him' for the added αὐτῷ.
ASV answers 'The first', rendering πρῶτος rather than ὕστερος ('the last').
English requires subject before prepositional phrase — 'For John came unto you' — so the Greek transposition leaves no trace.
ASV 'did not even repent yourselves' renders the ascensive οὐδέ, which plain οὐ would not supply.
ASV reads 'There was a man that was a householder' with no 'certain', so the added τις is unrendered.
σχῶμεν and κατάσχωμεν both yield ASV 'take his inheritance'; the compound adds nothing the English marks.
ASV prints verse 44 in the text with the note 'Some ancient authorities omit verse 44', so the omission r02 is excluded; r00-base and r01 are the same verse, r01 being its abbreviated citation.
ἐπεὶ εἰς and ἐπειδὴ ὡς are rendered alike by ASV 'because they took him for a prophet'.
